judgments.title: CMC I-CARE SDN BHD & ors v THEVAN REALTY & ors
judgments.catchwords: There are two applications before the Court. In Enclosure 45, the first and second defendants seek to strike out the plaintiff's action under Order 18 rule 19(1) (a), (b) and/or (d) of the Rules of Court 2012 ("ROC"), while Enclosure 48 is the same type of application filed by the third and fourth defendants. In the present suit, the first plaintiff seeks to set aside the judgment granted by the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court in Suit 691 in favour of the first defendant for the sum of RM225,000.00, together with costs and interest. Meanwhile, the second plaintiff also seeks to set aside the judgment granted by the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court in Suit 429 in which his claim against the first and second defendants for RM150,000.00 was dismissed with costs. The court finds that the current allegations are based entirely on documents that were already before the Sessions Court. To further compound the matter, there were no allegations of forgery in the Sessions Court despite the fact that the relevant documents were included in the Common Bundle of Documents. In fact, these documents were placed in part B at the proceedings in the Sessions Court, indicating their authenticity. Moreover, all the issues raised by the plaintiffs now could and should have been raised in the Sessions Court. Essentially, the plaintiffs are rehashing issues that have already been tried and decided by the Sessions Courts and the High Courts that have heard the appeals. In light of the above, the court allows both Enclosures 45 and 48 with costs of RM6,000.00 to each set of the defendants, subject to allocatur.
judgments.judge: YA Dato' Raja Ahmad Mohzanuddin Shah bin Raja Mohzan

judgments.catchwords: Review jurisdiction - Rule 137 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 -Inherent powers of Federal Court – All sentences passed to be in accordance with the law – Avoiding miscarriage of justice - Exceptional circumstances - Fresh evidence of prisoner’s death following whipping. Whether whipping is against Art. 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (“UDHR”) and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration in its prohibitions against CIDT - Whether whipping is against customary international law.

- Adakah defendan pertama dan defendan kedua cuai di dalam menyelenggarakan motor bas bernombor pendaftaran WFC 4948 sehingga menyebabkan kematian si mati? - Adakah defendan ketiga cuai dalam mengambil tindakan sewajarnya dalam menjaga keselamatan dan/atau kebajikan si mati seorang kanak-kanak yang berada dalam jagaan defendan ketiga? - Adakah kecuaian tersebut berpunca daripada pihak defendan pertama dan defendan kedua atau defendan ketiga atau pihak ketiga pertama dan pihak ketiga kedua atau disumbangcuai oleh semua pihak? - Adakah defendan keempat dan kelima bertanggungan secara vikarius (vicariously liability) terhadap tindakan-tindakan, peninggalan-peninggalan dan/atau kegagalan-kegagalan serta kecuaian defendan ketiga? - Berapakah jumlah gantirugi yang layak diterima oleh plaintif akibat kerugian yang dialami akibat kecuaian dalam kes ini? - Adakah terdapat sebarang kecuaian defendan kedua dalam menyelenggarakan motorbas bernombor pendaftaran WFC 4948 apabila ia telah mendapat kelulusan PUSPAKOM untuk digunakan di atas jalan dari 11.5.2019 sehingga 11.11.2019? - Adakah tuntutan di bawah gantirugi teladan dan gantirugi melampau dibenarkan di bawah Akta Pengangkutan Jalan Raya 1987 dan undang-undang lain dalam kes kemalangan jalanraya? - Adakah si mati sendiri telah cuai dan/atau sumbang cuai kerana gagal menjaga keselamatan diri sendiri semasa menumpang motorbas bernombor pendaftaran WFC 4948 pada hari kejadian tersebut? - Adakah pihak ketiga pertama dan kedua cuai mengambil tindakan sewajarnya dalam menjaga keselamatan dan/atau kebajikan si mati, seorang pelajar yang menyertai anjuran pihak ketiga pertama dan kedua pada masa material berada dalam jagaan pihak ketiga pertama dan kedua?

judgments.title: FRANCIS HO SEE SIN v TOH OOI PENG & ors
judgments.catchwords: Appeal against Sessions Court judgment – Judgment ordered for Appellant to pay Respondents for two separate claims – First judgment to indemnify the Respondent – Appellant director of company which requested loan – Second judgment was based on alleged promise by Appellant to pay rentals received by his son in Australia for properties belonging to the Respondents in Australia – Appeal against judgment for first claim dismissed – Appeal against judgment for second claim allowed – Respondents could not prove any claim against the Appellant’s son – No consideration given by the Respondents – Sessions Court judge erred as it is an unsustainable claim against the Appellant that should have been filed in Australia
